t: Which of the following pairs of years have identical calendars? A) 1911 and 1924 B) 1906 and 1912 C) 1914 and 1925 D) 1911 and 1929
e: Both 1914 & 1925 are non-leap. Gap = 11 years with 3 leap years (1916,1920,1924) in between. Total shift = 11+3 = 14, which is divisible by 7 → same starting day → identical calendars.

t: A person was born on 8 June 2011. What day of the week will be on his 25th birthday?

t: January 5 of a leap year is Wednesday. How many total Saturdays and Thursdays are there in February of that year?

t: What will be the product of the number of Sundays and Fridays in the month of February in the year 2020?

t: 5th of a month is Tuesday. This month has 31 days. What will be the 12th of next month?

t: Which of the following calendars will be the same as the calendar for the year 2009?
e: Calendar repetition rules: (1) If the given year's next leap year is 28 years later, calendar repeats. (2) If the previous year of the given year is a leap year, add 6 years for repetition. (3) Otherwise add 11 years (or the combination that sums total odd days to a multiple of 7). Since 2008 (year before 2009) is a leap year, add 6 → 2009+6 = 2015. So the calendar of 2015 matches 2009.

t: If 31 January 2022 was a Monday, what was the day on the same date 100 years ago?
e: In 100 years there are exactly 6 odd days (a well-known constant: 100 years = 5 odd days if it's not covering an extra leap adjustment; per this question's key, 100 years = 6 odd days here due to century leap-year counting). So the day 100 years ago = Monday − 6 odd days = Tuesday (going backward: Monday-1=Sunday, -2=Saturday, -3=Friday, -4=Thursday, -5=Wednesday, -6=Tuesday).

t: If 10 days before was a Sunday and 6 days after would be a Tuesday, then what day is it today?
e: 6 days before Tuesday = Wednesday. 10 days before Sunday: Sunday+7=Sunday (same day repeats every 7 days), so 10 days before is same as 3 days before Sunday = Wednesday. Both conditions independently give 'today' as Wednesday — a consistency-check trick question.

t: If it will be Monday the day after tomorrow, then what was the day of the week 50 days ago from today?

t: If 20 June of a particular year falls on the 6th day after Tuesday, then what will be the day on 11 August of the same year?

t: John bought a puppy on Friday, 21 January 2022. The puppy became an adult dog on the 380th day since John bought him. On which day did the puppy become an adult?
e: From 21 Jan 2022 to 21 Jan 2023 = 365 days = 1 odd day (2022 is not a leap year in this stretch). We need 380 days total, so 15 more days needed after 21 Jan 2023. 15 ÷ 7 = remainder 1. Total odd days = 1(first year)+1(extra 15 days) = 2. Required day = Friday + 2 = Sunday.

t: If the 20th day of the month falls on the 4th day before Monday, then what will be the day of the week on the 1st of that month?

We need to go back to the 1st (19 days back, or equivalently within the week cycle: 20th - 5 days = the day corresponding to date difference of 19, and 19 mod 7 = 5, so subtract 5 days). Thursday − 5 = Saturday. So the 1st of the month is Saturday.

t: If the seventh day of a month is three days earlier than Friday, then what day will it be on the 20th day of the month?

t: What will be the day on 31 December 2006 if 1 January 2006 is a Wednesday?

Since 1 January is already known to be Wednesday, we are concerned with the remaining days of the year. Now, (365 - 1) ÷ 7 = 364 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks. (which means 0 odd days) So, 31 December 2006 will be Wednesday. So, option (c) is the correct answer.

Thus, Tuesday - 2 days = Sunday

e: Years: 2028 - 2020 = 8 in which there are two leap years. t: If 17 April 1992 is Friday, then what will be the day of the week on 10 October 1993?
e: Total number of days from 17 April 1992 to 17 April 1993 = 365 days Total number of days from 17 April 1993 to 17 September 1993 = 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 = 153 days Total number of days from 17 September 1993 to 10 October 1993 = 23 days Total days = 365 + 153 + 23 = 541 days = 77 weeks 2 days Hence, the day on 10 October 1993 will be Sunday.
